sentences.text: Nodocephalosaurus was a large armored dinosaur estimated to reach 4.5 meters in length and weigh 1.5 tonnes. Its distinctive name means "knob-headed lizard," referring to the bulbous osteoderms fused to the top of its skull.

Robert M. Sullivan originally diagnosed the species by features including a prominent quadratojugal horn and a post-maxillary/lacrimal osteoderm. The squamosal horns arch towards the back and terminate in a rounded point.
In 2000, Tracy Ford assigned a single pup-tent scute to the genus, providing rare evidence of its skin texture.
The presence of this animal indicates that ankylosaurids were more diverse than nodosaurids in the San Juan Basin.

The only known specimen is a partial skull discovered in 1995 in the De-na-zin member of the Kirtland Formation in New Mexico. Robert M. Sullivan named Nodocephalosaurus in 1999 based on this find. The holotype specimen, which is the specimen the species is based on, is now housed at the State Museum of Pennsylvania in Harrisburg.
Six fossil occurrences of this genus have been recorded across the region.
Contemporary non-dinosaur species included a choristodere, crocodylomorphs like Denazinosuchus, several turtles, and fish such as Melvius and Myledaphus.

Vickaryous et al. (2004) interpreted Nodocephalosaurus as Ankylosauridae incertae sedis, meaning its exact position within the family was uncertain. It belongs to the subfamily Ankylosaurinae and is classified within the family Ankylosauridae. The animal is a member of the class Ornithischia.

Nodocephalosaurus fossils come from the De-na-zin member of the Kirtland Formation. The animal lived between 73.49 and 73.04 million years ago during the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian stages. It inhabited a floodplain on the western edge of the Western Interior Seaway rich in ferns, conifers, and flowering plants. Evidence suggests the environment had a warm temperate to subtropical climate.
Arbour and Currie (2015) assigned most referred Nodocephalosaurus specimens to Ankylosauridae indet. after discovering other ankylosaurids in the same formation.
